subject: Personnel proofs + redaction checklist for SOC 2 submission
messages:
From: Lauren Price <lprice@secureassess.io>
To: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: compliance@bluecrest.com
Date: 2028-05-30 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Personnel artifacts needed for SOC 2 / SIG submission

Hi Irene,

Thanks for agreeing to share personnel artifacts as part of the SOC 2 evidence bundle. To keep the auditor review moving, could you provide the following by EOD Tuesday, June 3:

- Representative training completion logs for the past 12 months (we usually request one month sample plus a rolling 12-month extract). CSV or PDF ok; include course IDs, completion dates, and role.
- Background check attestations or redacted summaries for three sample employees across different roles (engineer, sales rep, manager). Redaction guidance below.
- Deprovisioning checklist or offboarding timeline for any employees who left in the last 12 months (date of termination, timestamp of account disable, and last access).
- A short attestation from HR confirming training policy and frequency (one paragraph).

Redaction guidance we follow: mask PII (SSNs, passport numbers) and remove personal addresses; keep hashed employee IDs or unique internal IDs so we can match artifacts across files. If you prefer, we accept a brief cover letter describing the redaction method and a mapping table of hashed IDs to roles stored locally at Redwood.

Also attaching a sample evidence index and a CAIQ crosswalk to help map files to questions. Let me know if you need more time; we can negotiate a short extension but auditors prefer the June 3 cutoff.

Thanks,
Lauren
Senior Auditor
SecureAssess.io

Attachments referenced: evidence_index_template.xlsx, caiq_personnel_crosswalk.pdf

From: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Personnel artifacts needed for SOC 2 / SIG submission

Hi Lauren,

Appreciate the clear list — we can assemble these. Marissa and Ben from People Ops are on copy to pull training logs and offboarding timelines; Naomi is looped in for legal sign-off on what we can share for background checks.

Initial answers / plan:
- Training logs: we can produce a CSV extract for May 2028 and a rolling 12-month summary. We will remove direct PII (addresses, SSNs) and provide internal employee IDs hashed with SHA256 so auditors can correlate records.
- Background checks: we will provide redacted summaries that show check type, completion date, and a cleared/exception flag. No raw SSNs will be included. Naomi, please confirm if a short HR attestation is acceptable in lieu of original signed forms.
- Offboarding timeline: Ben will provide a spreadsheet with termination dates, account disable timestamps, and steps completed per our deprovisioning workflow.

We expect to have the package ready by EOD June 1 so you have a buffer before your June 3 deadline. If auditors need anything more granular, flag the specific questions and we will escalate.

I will attach a short cover note from HR once Naomi confirms wording.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Head of Compliance, Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.ai

> We expect to have the package ready by EOD June 1 so you have a buffer before your June 3 deadline.

Team — confirming People Ops can produce the following by EOD June 1:

1) training_completion_log_May2028.csv — includes: employee_hashed_id, role, course_id, course_name, completion_date, certificate_id (if issued). We will replace names/emails with hashed_id.
2) bg_check_summary_redacted.pdf — a one-page summary for three employees (engineer, account exec, manager) listing check performed (criminal, employment verification), date completed, and result (cleared/exception). No DOB, SSN, or address will be included. Where checks flagged a minor discrepancy, we'll include a brief note on remediation status.
3) offboarding_deprovision_report_2027-2028.xlsx — rows for each leaver in past 12 months with columns: employee_hashed_id, termination_date, account_disabled_at (UTC), last_login, deprovision_steps_completed.

Question for Legal / Compliance: Naomi, is a signed attestation from our HR Director plus a separate one-paragraph CISO attestation sufficient for the SOC 2 evidence pack, or do the auditors insist on original background vendor reports (redacted)?

Ben and I will prepare the redaction checklist we used and include a short narrative describing the hashing approach.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, People Operations
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: Lauren Price <lprice@secureassess.io>
To: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: compliance@bluecrest.com, auditor@secureassess.io
Date: 2028-05-31 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Personnel artifacts needed for SOC 2 / SIG submission

Irene, Marissa —

Thanks for the quick turn. That plan sounds good and the June 1 delivery will work. A few clarifications before you send:

- Hashed employee IDs are acceptable; please note the hashing algorithm and salt approach in the cover note so the auditor can verify uniqueness.
- Redacted background summaries are sufficient for initial review. If the auditor escalates, we may ask for vendor-transmitted reports under an NDA, but please do not send vendor originals now.
- The attestation: a signed paragraph from HR plus a CISO attestation is perfect. We prefer both signatures on a single PDF but two separate signed PDFs are fine.

Please upload artifacts to the shared Drive link you included or reply with a secure transfer link. Once received, I'll confirm completeness and open any follow-up tickets with the audit team.

If you can include a short mapping table (hashed_id -> role) that's non-PII, that makes correlating items much faster.

Best,
Lauren Price
Senior Auditor, SecureAssess.io

Received after desk review: please include your internal evidence index filename in the metadata when uploading so we can reference in the CAIQ crosswalk.
